How old was Victoria when she became Queen?
Why couldn't Victoria be Queen of Hanover?
answers: 'I will be good'
Eighteen
Hanover's law did not allow a woman to rule

lessons.title: Chapter 102: Victoria – When Bread Was Dear
steps: Read chapter 102 aloud together
Narrate why bread was so dear and how the Irish potato famine came about
Find Ireland on a map of the British Isles
Add 'Irish potato famine begins, 1845' and 'Corn Laws repealed, 1846' to your timeline
questions: What did the Corn Laws forbid?
What food did most poor Irish people live on?
Which country across the sea sent help to Ireland?
answers: Bringing in foreign corn until British corn was very dear
Potatoes
The United States
lessons.notes: The famine description includes starving children; about a million died and many more emigrated, which the book only touches on.

lessons.title: Chapter 103: Victoria – Peace
steps: Read chapter 103 aloud together
Narrate Prince Albert's idea for the Great Exhibition and how the Crystal Palace was built
Find Hyde Park on a map of London
Add 'Great Exhibition in the Crystal Palace, 1851' to your timeline
questions: What did Prince Albert hope the Exhibition would do?
Who thought of building with glass and iron?
What did people call the building?
answers: Help world trade and make nations friendlier
Sir Joseph Paxton
The Crystal Palace
lessons.notes: The book says the Crystal Palace still stands; it burned down in 1936.

lessons.title: Chapter 104: Victoria – War
steps: Read chapter 104 aloud together
Narrate Florence Nightingale's work in the hospitals and the Charge of the Light Brigade
Find the Crimea, the Black Sea, and Sebastopol (Sevastopol) on a map
Add 'Crimean War and the Charge of the Light Brigade, 1854' to your timeline
questions: What strange mistake was made with a shipload of boots?
Why was Florence Nightingale called 'the lady with the lamp'?
Why did the Light Brigade charge the Russian guns?
answers: They were all for the left foot
She walked the wards at night with a lamp, caring for the men
An order was misunderstood
lessons.notes: The book credits Nightingale with the red cross badge; the Red Cross was actually founded by Henri Dunant in 1863.

lessons.title: Chapter 105: Victoria – The Land of Snow
steps: Read chapter 105 aloud together
Narrate Franklin's voyage and how searchers finally learned what happened to his men
Find the Arctic Ocean and northern Canada on a globe or world map
Add 'Franklin's Arctic expedition sets out, 1845' to your timeline
questions: What were Franklin's two ships called?
How did searchers try to send messages using foxes?
Who kept urging the search for Franklin?
answers: The Terror and the Erebus
They put copper collars with directions on white foxes
Lady Franklin, his wife
lessons.notes: The book uses the older word 'Eskimos' (Inuit). Both ships' wrecks were finally found in 2014 and 2016, which children may enjoy looking up.

lessons.title: Chapter 106: Victoria – The Siege of Delhi
steps: Read chapter 106 aloud together (parent may wish to preview)
Narrate why the sepoys refused the new cartridges and how the rising began at Meerut
Find Meerut, Delhi, and Cawnpore (Kanpur) on a map of India
Add 'Indian Rebellion (the 'Mutiny') begins, 1857' to your timeline
questions: Why did the sepoys refuse to use the new cartridges?
Where did the rising first break out?
Whom did the sepoys want to make their Emperor again?
answers: They believed the grease was cow and pig fat, against their religions
Meerut
The old Mughal Emperor at Delhi
lessons.notes: The Cawnpore massacre of women and children is described in grim detail; preview it. The book tells only the British side; Indians remember 1857 as a war of independence, and British reprisals were also brutal.

lessons.title: Chapter 107: Victoria – The Pipes at Lucknow
steps: Read chapter 107 aloud together
Narrate the siege of the Residency and how Jessie heard the pipes
Find Lucknow and the Gomti (Goomtee) River on a map of India
Add 'Relief of Lucknow, 1857' and 'Crown takes over rule of India, 1858' to your timeline
questions: What did Sir Henry Lawrence tell his men before he died?
What sound did Jessie hear?
Who became the first Viceroy of India?
answers: Never yield; die at your post rather than yield
The Highland bagpipes of the relieving army
Lord Canning
lessons.notes: The story of Jessie's dream is a popular legend of the time and may not be literally true. The poem's 'Indian tiger' language reflects a colonial viewpoint.

units.title: Unit 13: Empire and the Twentieth Century (Chapters 108–114)

lessons.title: Chapter 108: Victoria – Under the Southern Cross
steps: Read chapter 108 aloud together
Narrate how the first convict colony at Sydney nearly starved and how Governor Phillip shared his food
Find Botany Bay and Sydney on a map of Australia
Add 'Cook lands at Botany Bay, 1770' and 'First Fleet founds Sydney, 1788' to your timeline
questions: Why did Cook name the place Botany Bay?
Why were convicts sent to Australia instead of America?
What did Governor Phillip do with his own flour?
answers: There were so many kinds of plants
America had been lost as a colony
He gave it up to share with everyone
lessons.notes: The book calls Aboriginal Australians 'savages' and ignores that the land was already their home; a short talk about Aboriginal peoples and the effects of colonization is worthwhile.

lessons.title: Chapter 109: Victoria – From Cannibal to Christian
steps: Read chapter 109 aloud together (see parent note)
Narrate the meeting at Waitangi and what the chiefs said for and against the treaty
Find North Island, South Island, and Waitangi on a map of New Zealand
Add 'Treaty of Waitangi, 1840' to your timeline
questions: What missionary bought land in New Zealand for twelve axes?
What did the chief who opposed the treaty fear?
How did most chiefs sign the treaty?
answers: Marsden
That they would become slaves and lose their land
With marks like their tattoo patterns
lessons.notes: The chapter title and text describe the Maori in demeaning colonial terms. The Treaty of Waitangi is still debated today, as its English and Maori versions differ and land was later taken.

lessons.title: Chapter 110: Victoria – Boer and Briton
steps: Read chapter 110 aloud together
Narrate the main causes of the Boer War and how peace was made at Vereeniging
Find Cape Town, Kimberley, Ladysmith, and Mafeking (Mahikeng) on a map of South Africa
Add 'Boer War, 1899–1902' and 'Death of Queen Victoria, 1901' to your timeline
questions: Who were the Uitlanders and what right were they denied?
Which three besieged towns were relieved?
How long did Queen Victoria reign?
answers: Mostly British newcomers in the Transvaal; the right to vote
Kimberley, Ladysmith, and Mafeking
Sixty-three years
lessons.notes: The book tells the war from the British side and leaves out the black African population and the British concentration camps where many Boer and African civilians died.

lessons.title: Chapter 111: Edward VII – The Peacemaker
steps: Read chapter 111 aloud together
Narrate why Edward VII was called the Peacemaker and what happened before his coronation
Find Paris, Rome, Vienna, and The Hague on a map of Europe
Add 'Coronation of Edward VII, 1902' and 'Entente Cordiale with France, 1904' to your timeline
questions: Why was Edward's coronation delayed?
What did the French call King Edward?
What was the Hague Court set up to do?
answers: He fell dangerously ill and needed an operation
The Uncle of Europe
Settle quarrels between nations by arbitration instead of war
lessons.notes: Written just after World War I, the chapter is strongly anti-German; you might point out how wartime feelings shaped the author's view.

lessons.title: Chapter 112: George V. – Armed Peace
steps: Read chapter 112 aloud together
Narrate the chain of events from the shooting at Sarajevo to Britain declaring war
Find Sarajevo in Bosnia, Serbia, and Belgium on a map of Europe
Add 'Archduke Franz Ferdinand shot at Sarajevo, June 1914' and 'Britain enters the war, 4 August 1914' to your timeline
questions: Who was shot at Sarajevo?
Which neutral country did Germany march through?
What did the German Chancellor call the treaty protecting Belgium?
answers: Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria and his wife
Belgium
'A scrap of paper'
lessons.notes: The causes of WWI are presented one-sidedly, putting all blame on Germany and Austria; historians today give a more shared picture.

lessons.title: Chapter 113: World War
steps: Read chapter 113 aloud together
Narrate how life in Britain changed during the war, including women's work and rationing
Find Flanders in Belgium, northern France, and Jutland (Denmark) on a map of Europe
Add 'USA joins the war, April 1917' and 'Armistice, 11 November 1918' to your timeline
questions: What kind of fighting happened along the long line in France and Belgium?
How did women help at home during the war?
What helped bring the United States into the war?
answers: Trench warfare
They took over jobs in factories, farms, offices, and transport
Germany's submarines sinking ships, including neutral ones
lessons.notes: Mentions poison gas, air raids, and huge losses; the tone is strongly wartime-British. Older children may want to talk about how ordinary soldiers on both sides suffered.

lessons.title: Chapter 114: The Hope of the Future
steps: Read the final chapter aloud together (skip the list of kings at the end)
Narrate what the League of Nations was meant to do and how the author compares nations to growing children
Find Geneva in Switzerland and Paris, where the peace conference met, on a map of Europe
Add 'Treaty of Versailles, 28 June 1919' and 'League of Nations founded, 1920' to your timeline
questions: Which country appeared again as an independent state after the war?
Where was the League of Nations to have its permanent office?
What did League members promise to do before going to war?
answers: Poland
Geneva
Bring their quarrel to the League and give it time to settle it peacefully
lessons.notes: The League failed to prevent World War II; you might close the book by mentioning the United Nations, which replaced it in 1945.
